task.title: Reduce redundant generation and runtime work
task.source: Direct user request to implement all high-impact lossless De-Koi optimizations.
task.classification: prompt assembly, storage reads, integration availability, attachment delivery, and bundle loading

coreClaim: De-Koi performs less repeated storage, bridge, provider, attachment, and bundle work without changing generated text, tracker precedence, attachment ordering, compatibility behavior, or user-visible capabilities.
rootCause: Several hot paths independently reloaded immutable turn data, transferred full histories to select one row, probed Spotify through the provider, resolved duplicate images sequentially, or coupled drag-and-drop with broadly used motion code.

inScope: Separate motion and drag-and-drop vendor chunks
Reuse one ordered regex-script snapshot per generation
Check Spotify playback availability from local credentials
Select tracker snapshots at the Rust storage boundary
Deduplicate and bound stored image attachment resolution
outOfScope: Changing generated prompt text or regex ordering
Changing Spotify authorization or playback behavior
Changing tracker persistence or snapshot schema
Changing attachment size limits or warning copy
Adding new user-facing settings or workflows

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: Generation and runtime consumers repeatedly paid for data or dependencies whose value was stable for the operation, while selection logic crossed owner boundaries with full histories.
contractLaneGate.producer: Engine generation orchestration, Rust tracker and Spotify capabilities, attachment delivery, and Vite vendor chunk configuration
contractLaneGate.consumer: Foreground and dry-run generation, conversation command prompting, tracker restoration, historical image prompts, and lazy application surfaces
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: An operation should reuse one stable snapshot or return one owner-selected result without changing ordering, fallbacks, compatibility, warnings, or visible behavior.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: Generation caches one ordered regex snapshot, Rust returns focused availability and tracker selection results, attachment resolution deduplicates references behind a four-worker pool, and motion and drag-and-drop build into separate chunks.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: src/engine owns per-turn snapshot lifetime and attachment delivery ordering; src-tauri owns local tracker selection and Spotify credential facts; docs/workflow owns only the evidence ledger.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not add per-caller caches, UI flags, provider probes, or mode-specific selection copies; each optimization belongs at the stable producer or owner boundary.
regressionProof: One regex list call is asserted across input, prompt, reassembly, and output.
Spotify availability asserts the focused local capability is called and the player is not.
Rust tracker tests cover visible, committed, exclusion, fallback, and legacy yes precedence.
Attachment tests cover deduplication, four-worker bounds, stable ordering, warnings, and earliest failure.
The production manifest proves AppExperience imports motion without drag-and-drop.

groundTruthFacts.evidence: The focused Rust capability and TypeScript gateway tests cover configured and missing local credentials while asserting the player is not called.

userActionCopy.description: No migration or cleanup is required. Optional rollback protection before Pi deployment is a stopped-app copy of the existing De-Koi data directory.

reviewThreadLedger.finding: Bunny found that malformed tracker rows could remain eligible in the new Rust-side selector.
reviewThreadLedger.fix: The Rust selector now requires the same parseable messageId and swipeIndex target as the previous TypeScript list path and compares normalized target tuples. Focused tests prove malformed rows are skipped and whitespace-padded legacy message ids still match visible anchors.

reviewThreadLedger.finding: Bunny suggested converting a rejected image resolver into a partial-success warning.
reviewThreadLedger.fix: The pre-optimization sequential implementation propagated any resolver rejection. The concurrent implementation intentionally preserves that contract while collecting outcomes first so the earliest rejected input, not the fastest rejection, is thrown.

reviewThreadLedger.finding: Bunny questioned whether deduplicated image references preserve group-local images and warnings.
reviewThreadLedger.fix: Each group is reconstructed from its original attachment positions after shared resolution. The focused jagged-group test proves a repeated resolved image is delivered to both groups and a missing image warns only in the group containing it.

reviewThreadLedger.finding: Bunny suggested the concurrent resolver could surface the fastest failure instead of the earliest input failure.
reviewThreadLedger.fix: Workers record outcomes without rejecting Promise.all, then delivery walks groups and attachments in input order. A focused controlled-race test proves a slower first input failure is surfaced before a faster later failure.

reviewThreadLedger.finding: Bunny suggested adding fallback and row filtering to the extracted regex-script loader.
reviewThreadLedger.fix: The previous implementation used the same storage.list result and propagated storage errors; invalid regex expressions were and remain ignored at application time. Adding a fallback would hide a storage failure and change the lossless refactor contract.

verification.baselineEvidence: 2702 frontend tests, the full serialized Rust workspace, 108 focused tests, repository checks, strict Clippy, production bundle budgets, and whitespace validation passed.
